newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB sees share split news before year-end.
newsitem.headline: UCB sees share split news before year-end.

text.p: Belgian chemicals, drugs and films group UCB said on Wednesday that it was studying splitting its shares and that concrete proposals would be put to shareholders before the end of the year.

"A decision will be taken before the end of the year," UCB spokesman Alain Douxchamps told Reuters. A split was being considered at the request of small shareholders and UCB employees for whom the shares were expensive at current prices.
UCB stock breached the 100,000 franc level on Tuesday, closing at 100,800 francs, off an intraday high of 102,000 francs also set on Tuesday.
The share has been a runaway hit. Two years ago it was at 26,825 francs, one year ago at 59,300.
Profits at UCB, a Belgian-based successful niche player, more than doubled in the last five years, reaching 5.6 billion francs in 1996. The company is forecasting further growth.
Sales grew from 47.13 billion francs in 1992 to 50.83 billion in 1996. Financial charges were cut to 530 million francs in 1996 from 1.21 billion in 1992.
The company's largest contributor to pre-tax profits is drugs, its current star product anti-allergy drug Zyrtec.
Douxchamps made the comments on the stock split after UCB said earlier on Wednesday it would buy a cellulose film production unit from U.S. firm Flexel Inc.
UCB told shareholders on Tuesday it expected ordinary profits to continue to grow in 1997, noting prospects remained "very favourable" in its three sectors.
Analysts said the comments sounded more optimistic than those in April when the company spoke only of "favourable" prospects.

"It is especially the case for the film division (10 percent of total current results in 1996) whose sales and results are poised for a strong improvement," Generale Bank said in its daily research note.
The bank expected UCB to take a decision on the share split in the coming month.
